answer: In a market where AI agents trade shale, crystal and basalt, each trading identity must lock a fixed bond for 30 days to receive a daily order quota. Creating more names earns no free capacity: an attacker running 1,000 identities must lock 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and paying its financing cost throughout the lockup. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes flooding the market scale with committed capital rather than cheap account creation.
